title: 64 Estimating enteric methane emissions in grazing livestock: a practical approach with fecal NIRS/Nutbal System
content:
Abstract
Traditional approaches for quantifying enteric methane (CH₄) often rely on controlled environments or costly technologies, which may not reflect the complexity of grazing systems or their practical applicability on commercial operations. The Grazingland Animal Nutrition Laboratory has utilized fecal near infrared reflectance spectroscopy (FNIRS) since 1995 to support strategic livestock nutrition management. We explored the potential of FNIRS to estimate CH₄ emissions for grazing beef cattle and provide producers with tools for optimizing sustainable management practices. Using a comprehensive dataset of over 30,000 samples from across the U.S., we selected a subset (n = 1,586) representing cattle grazing in Eastern and Southern Texas (TX) and Eastern New Mexico (NM). Monthly means for diet crude protein (CP) and diet digestible organic matter (DOM) were derived from data aggregated over 1993 to 2007. Diet indicators and animal characteristics were input into the Nutritional Balance Analyzer (Nutbal) to generate animal performance metrics, including feed intake (FI). FI estimates (kg DM/animal/day) were applied to established CH₄ prediction equations to estimate methane emissions across cow-calf and stocker systems, reflecting real-world scenarios. Angus, and Brahman-crossbred steers (8 months, BCS = 6), and Angus, and Brahman-crossbred cows (60 months, 40 days lactating, BCS = 5) were utilized in Nutbal. Differences among estimations were assessed through ANOVA, with significance determined at P < 0.05. CP varied from 8.33% to 14.36% in TX and 6.44 to 10.10% in NM (P < 0.01), while DOM varied from 59.79% to 65.69% in TX and 58.15% to 62.83% in NM (P < 0.01). FI estimates varied seasonally across regions (P < 0.01), however, no differences were attributed to breed type in the model predictions (P > 0.01). Steers in TX exhibited average FI ranging from 5.33 to 10.46 kg DM/day, while FI in NM steers ranged from 4.34 to 9.86 kg DM/day (P = 0.08). Cows in TX had FI ranging from 12.52 to 14.58 kg DM/day, while FI in NM cows was between 11.32 to 13.98 kg DM/day (P < 0.01). As expected, methane emissions (CH₄, kg/animal/day) exhibited similar seasonal patterns as FI. In TX, CH₄ emissions from steers varied from 0.16 to 0.33 kg/day, while NM steers ranged from 0.12 to 0.31 kg/day (P = 0.08). Cows in TX had emissions ranging from 0.41 to 0.48 kg/day while in NM, cows exhibited CH₄ emissions between 0.36 and 0.46 kg/day (P < 0.01). The FNIRS/Nutbal System provides a non-invasive and accessible tool for enhancing models that estimate CH₄ emissions from grazing cattle. By offering region-specific guidance, this system empowers ranchers and extension professionals to align productivity goals with environmental stewardship. Further validation against CH₄ reference methods will enhance its reliability in advancing sustainable livestock systems and climate-smart grazing practices.
